value.name: Asha pulls deed list closer
value.description: Asha subtly draws the deed list toward her side of the desk while pressing Daniel to identify the house entry.
evidence: Asha drew the deed list a fraction closer to her side of the desk and asked him, in the same level voice she had used over the watermark, to put his finger on the entry for the house itself.

value.name: Daniel sits uneasily
value.description: Daniel lowers himself into the chair without fully settling, signaling continued tension and alertness.
evidence: Daniel lowered himself into the chair without quite settling into it, his weight still forward

value.name: Daniel scans the deed list nervously
value.description: Daniel looks over the page without focusing, while his attention drifts toward the open study door and the hall beyond.
evidence: his eyes traveled the page without landing
his glance went briefly to the open study door and the length of hall beyond it before returning to the paper

value.name: Asha withholds immediate explanation
value.description: Asha lets silence linger, forcing Daniel to confront the line she wants him to read.
evidence: Asha let the silence sit a beat longer than was comfortable before she tapped the line for the title and waited for him to read it aloud

value.name: Asha challenges Daniel's urgency
value.description: Asha asks why the line requires so much specificity from Daniel before Thursday and insists on hearing the title read aloud.
evidence: Asha kept her eyes on Daniel and asked him, in the same even register, why this particular line wanted so much specificity from him before Thursday; she would rather, she said, hear the title read out than paraphrase it for him

value.name: Daniel reads the house entry aloud
value.description: Daniel finally points to the line and reads the deed entry in a careful, lawyerly tone that makes the conveyance sound unsettled.
evidence: Daniel's finger came down on the line a moment later than it should have, and he read the entry aloud in a careful, half-lawyered voice, the words about the house and its conveyance to him sounding less settled in his mouth than they did on the page
